q: In Grade 10, one dimensional motion such as ____ and free fall motion was studied.
e: Grade 10 stayed on one axis: linear motion and free fall. In Grade 10, one dimensional motion such as linear motion and free fall motion was studied.

q: It is expected that students will examine two-dimensional motion; projectile and ____ motion.
e: The two standard plane motions in this chapter are projectile motion and circular motion. Two-dimensional motion; projectile and circular motion.

q: In this chapter we will consider motion in two dimensions (or) motion in a ____.
e: Two-dimensional motion is motion in a plane. Motion in two dimensions (or) motion in a plane.

q: The object may move in both the x and ____ direction simultaneously.
e: The object is free to change x and y at the same time. The object may move in both the x and y direction simultaneously.

q: In order to describe the motion of an object in two dimensions, ____ concept must be used.
e: You need the vector idea because direction matters as well as size. In order to describe the motion of an object in two dimensions, vector concept must be used.

q: The object moves along a ____ path between points P and Q as shown in Figure 1.1.
e: Between P and Q the object follows a curve, so the displacement is the straight vector Δr, not the path length. The object moves along a curved path between points P and Q as shown in Figure 1.1.

q: The displacement vector of the object from P to Q is ____.
e: The change of position from P to Q is the displacement vector Δr. The displacement vector of the object from P to Q is Δr.

q: The perpendicular components of $\Delta \vec{r}$ are ____ and $\Delta y$.
e: Δr splits into a horizontal piece Δx and a vertical piece Δy. The perpendicular components of Δr are Δx and Δy.

q: The magnitude of $\Delta \vec{r}$ is given by $|\Delta \vec{r}| = $ ____.
e: The size of Δr is the Pythagorean root of Δx² plus Δy². You do not add Δx and Δy raw, and you do not subtract the squares. The magnitude of Δr is given by |Δr| = √((Δx)² + (Δy)²).

q: To find the direction of $\Delta \vec{r}$, $\tan \theta = $ ____.
e: The direction angle uses opposite over adjacent: tan θ = Δy/Δx. To find the direction of Δr, tan θ = (Δy)/(Δx).

q: Average velocity is defined as $\vec{v}_{avg} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} $ ____.
e: Average velocity is displacement over the time interval, Δr/Δt. Average velocity is defined as vavg = limitΔt → 0 (Δr)/(Δt).

q: Instantaneous velocity is defined as $\vec{v} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \vec{r}}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of Δr/Δt as Δt goes to zero, which is dr/dt. Instantaneous velocity is defined as v = limitΔt → 0 (Δr)/(Δt) = (dr)/(dt).

q: Average acceleration is given by $\vec{a}_{avg} = $ ____.
e: Average acceleration is the change of velocity over the time interval, Δv/Δt. Average acceleration is given by aavg = (Δv)/(Δt).

q: Instantaneous acceleration is defined as $\vec{a} = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \vec{v}}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Instantaneous acceleration is the limit of Δv/Δt, which is dv/dt. (dv)/(dt) is what this sentence is naming.

q: An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is ____ as the direction of the velocity is changing.
e: An object moving with constant speed along a curved path is accelerating as the direction of the velocity is changing. Accelerating is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the velocity of the object is ____ to its path.
e: The velocity arrow stays tangent to the path. The direction of the velocity of the object is tangential to its path.

q: Hence, the object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in magnitude, ____, (or) both.
e: Acceleration is a change of the velocity vector: size, direction, or both. Hence, the object is accelerated whenever the velocity changes in magnitude, direction, (or) both.

q: An object moves in both x and y direction simultaneously is said to be undergoing ____ motion.
e: The object is free to change x and y at the same time. An object moves in both x and y direction simultaneously is said to be undergoing projectile motion.

q: Circular motion is a movement of an object along the ____ of a circle or rotation along a circular path.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. Circular motion is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle or rotation along a circular path.

q: Instantaneous angular velocity is defined as the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Displacement is what this sentence is naming.

q: Instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Velocity is what this sentence is naming. Velocity is the term used with Instantaneous angular acceleration time rate change.

q: A projectile is any object thrown into space upon which the only acting force is the ____.
e: A projectile, air resistance ignored, feels only gravity. A projectile is any object thrown into space upon which the only acting force is the gravity.

q: The path followed by a projectile is known as a ____.
e: A projectile's path is called its trajectory. The path followed by a projectile is known as a trajectory.

q: The motion of an object moving in both horizontal x direction and vertical y direction simultaneously is called the ____.
e: That x-and-y motion is projectile motion. The motion of an object moving in both horizontal x direction and vertical y direction simultaneously is called the projectile motion.

q: If air resistance is neglected, an object moves along the horizontal x direction with a constant ____ and in the vertical y direction with constant downward acceleration.
e: With no air resistance the horizontal velocity stays constant. Acceleration is zero along x, not constant and nonzero. If air resistance is neglected, an object moves along the horizontal x direction with a constant velocity and in the vertical y direction with constant downward acceleration.

q: In such case, only ____ force is acting on it.
e: A projectile, air resistance ignored, feels only gravity. In such case, only gravitational force is acting on it.

q: Therefore, the downward acceleration is the acceleration due to ____ which is a constant over the range of motion.
e: The downward acceleration is g, constant near the ground. Therefore, the downward acceleration is the acceleration due to gravity which is a constant over the range of motion.

q: The vertical motion of projectile is a ____ motion.
e: Vertical projectile motion is uniformly accelerated motion under g. The vertical motion of projectile is a free fall motion.

q: If the initial velocity makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal, the x and y components of the initial velocity are $v_{0x} = $ ____ and $v_{0y} = v_0 \sin \theta$.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. If the initial velocity makes an angle θ with the horizontal, the x and y components of the initial velocity are v0x = v_0 cos θ and v0y = v_0 sin θ.

q: In order to analyze the projectile motion, the motion can be considered into two parts, horizontal motion (x direction) and ____ motion (y direction).
e: Treat a projectile as two motions: x with ax = 0 and y with ay = −g. In order to analyze the projectile motion, the motion can be considered into two parts, horizontal motion (x direction) and vertical motion (y direction).

q: In x direction, $a_x = 0$ and $v_x = v_{0x} = $ ____ $= \text{constant}$.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. In x direction, a_x = 0 and v_x = v0x = v_0 cos θ = constant.

q: The horizontal displacement of projectile can be written as a function of time; $x = v_{0x} t = $ ____.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. The horizontal displacement of projectile can be written as a function of time; x = v0x t = (v_0 cos θ) t.

q: In y direction, $v_{0y}$ is the initial velocity and $a_y$ is ____.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. In y direction, v0y is the initial velocity and a_y is -g.

q: Since the acceleration along the vertical y direction is downward direction, g can be taken as ____ sign.
e: Take upward as positive and ay = −g. Then vy = v0 sin θ − gt. Since the acceleration along the vertical y direction is downward direction, g can be taken as negative sign.

q: The velocity of the projectile in the time t in the y direction is given by $v_y = v_{0y} + $ ____.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. The velocity of the projectile in the time t in the y direction is given by v_y = v0y + a_y t.

q: The relation between vertical velocity and displacement is $v_y^2 = v_{0y}^2 + $ ____.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. The relation between vertical velocity and displacement is v_y² = v0y² + 2 a_y y.

q: The vertical displacement of the projectile in time t is given by $y = v_{0y} t + $ ____.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. The vertical displacement of the projectile in time t is given by y = v0y t + (1)/(2) a_y t².

q: The magnitude of the velocity of the projectile at any instant of time is, $v = $ ____.
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The magnitude of the velocity of the projectile at any instant of time is, v = √(v_x² + v_y²).

q: The direction of the velocity of the projectile is given by $\tan \theta = $ ____.
e: The direction angle uses opposite over adjacent: tan θ = Δy/Δx. The direction of the velocity of the projectile is given by tan θ = (v_y)/(v_x).

q: The projectile reaches the highest point when its vertical component of velocity ____ is zero.
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. The projectile reaches the highest point when its vertical component of velocity v_y is zero.

q: The time taken to reach the highest point is $t_1 = $ ____.
e: The time taken to reach the highest point is t_1 = (v_0 sin θ)/(g). Leave the relation as (v_0 sin θ)/(g).

q: The ____ is twice the time to reach the maximum height.
e: Maximum height uses only the vertical launch component: H = (v0 sinθ)² / 2g. The time of flight is twice the time to reach the maximum height.

q: The time of flight is given by $T = 2 t_1 = $ ____.
e: Time of flight is the whole time in the air, 2 v0 sinθ / g for landing at the same level. The time of flight is given by T = 2 t_1 = (2 v_0 sin θ)/(g).

q: The horizontal range R is the horizontal distance from the starting point to the point where the projectile returns to the same ____.
e: Range on level ground is v0² sin 2θ / g, largest at 45°. The horizontal range R is the horizontal distance from the starting point to the point where the projectile returns to the same height.

q: The horizontal range is obtained as $R = v_{0x} T = $ ____.
e: Range on level ground is v0² sin 2θ / g, largest at 45°. The horizontal range is obtained as R = v0x T = v_0 cos θ (2 v_0 sin θ)/(g).

q: Using the trigonometric identity $2 \sin \theta \cos \theta = \sin 2\theta$, the horizontal range is simplified to $R = $ ____.
e: Range on level ground is v0² sin 2θ / g, largest at 45°. Using the trigonometric identity 2 sin θ cos θ = sin 2θ, the horizontal range is simplified to R = (v_0² sin 2θ)/(g).

q: Another case of the projectile motion is an object thrown ____.
e: Split the projectile into constant-vx horizontal motion and ay = −g vertical motion. Another case of the projectile motion is an object thrown horizontally.

q: There is no vertical component to its initial velocity; that is, ____ $= 0$, $v_{0x} = v_0$.
e: Resolve the launch velocity: v0x = v0 cos θ and v0y = v0 sin θ. There is no vertical component to its initial velocity; that is, v0y = 0, v0x = v_0.

q: The vertical velocity of the object in the time t is $v_y = $ ____.
e: The vertical velocity of the object in the time t is v_y = -gt. -gt is what this statement is using.

q: The vertical displacement in time t for an object thrown horizontally is, $y = $ ____.
e: The vertical displacement in time t for an object thrown horizontally is, y = -(1)/(2)gt². Leave the relation as -(1)/(2)gt².

q: Circular motion is a specific type of a ____ motion.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. Circular motion is a specific type of a two-dimensional motion.

q: It is a movement of an object along the ____ of a circle (or) rotation along a circular path.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. It is a movement of an object along the circumference of a circle (or) rotation along a circular path.

q: We can experience a pulling force (known as the ____) exerted on the ball by the string.
e: We can experience a pulling force (known as the tension) exerted on the ball by the string. The name used here is tension.

q: Other examples of the circular motion are a satellite orbiting the earth, motion of a wheel, turning of a car around ____ respectively.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. Other examples of the circular motion are a satellite orbiting the earth, motion of a wheel, turning of a car around curved path respectively.

q: If an object (rigid body) rotates about an axis, each particle consisting of the object moves in a ____ motion.
e: If an object (rigid body) rotates about an axis, each particle consisting of the object moves in a circular motion. Circular is what this statement is using.

q: Although an object moves in a circle at a constant speed, its ____ is not constant.
e: Although an object moves in a circle at a constant speed, its velocity is not constant. Velocity is what this statement is using.

q: The direction of the velocity is ____ to the path.
e: The direction of the velocity is tangential to the path. Tangential is what this statement is using.

q: Velocity is constantly changing because the ____ of the velocity is changing continuously.
e: Velocity is constantly changing because the direction of the velocity is changing continuously. Direction is what this statement is using.

q: The velocity in circular motion is also called the ____ velocity.
e: In circular motion the object stays on a circle. The velocity is tangent and the centripetal acceleration points to the centre. The velocity in circular motion is also called the tangential velocity.

q: In this time interval, it has rotated through an angle $\theta$ with respect to the reference line and through a distance s measured along the circumference of the circle, called an ____ length.
e: In this time interval, it has rotated through an angle θ with respect to the reference line and through a distance s measured along the circumference of the circle, called an arc length. The name used here is arc.

q: Change of the angular position is called the angular ____.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. Change of the angular position is called the angular displacement.

q: The angular displacement is the ratio of the arc length to ____.
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. The angular displacement is the ratio of the arc length to radius.

q: The magnitude of angular displacement ($\theta$), measured in radian (rad), is given by $\theta = $ ____.
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. The magnitude of angular displacement (θ), measured in radian (rad), is given by θ = (s)/(r).

q: One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the ____ of the circle.
e: One radian is the angle at the centre when the arc length equals the radius. One radian is defined as the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle.

q: If $s = r$, $\theta = $ ____.
e: If s = r, θ = 1 radian. 1 radian is what this statement is using.
1 rev = 360° = 2π rad. 2π is what this statement is using.

q: Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to ____ taken.
e: Angular displacement is the angle swept, θ = s/r in radians. Average angular velocity is the ratio of the change in angular displacement to time taken.

q: Average angular velocity is given by $\omega_{avg} = \frac{\theta_2 - \theta_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Average angular velocity is given by ωavg = (θ_2 - θ_1)/(t_2 - t_1) = (Δθ)/(Δt).

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular velocity can be written as $\omega = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \theta}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. If the time interval Δt approaches zero, the instantaneous angular velocity can be written as ω = limitΔt → 0 (Δθ)/(Δt) = (dθ)/(dt).

q: At constant angular velocity, $\omega = $ ____.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. At constant angular velocity, ω = (θ)/(t).

q: Angular velocity is measured in radian per second (rad s$^{-1}$), revolution per second (rps) and revolution per ____ (rpm or rev min$^{-1}$).
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. Angular velocity is measured in radian per second (rad s^-1), revolution per second (rps) and revolution per minute (rpm or rev min^-1).

q: The average angular acceleration is the ratio of change of angular velocity to ____ taken.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The average angular acceleration is the ratio of change of angular velocity to time taken.

q: The average angular acceleration is given by $\alpha_{avg} = \frac{\omega_2 - \omega_1}{t_2 - t_1} = $ ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. The average angular acceleration is given by αavg = (ω_2 - ω_1)/(t_2 - t_1) = (Δω)/(Δt).

q: If the time interval $\Delta t$ approaches zero, the instantaneous angular acceleration can be defined as $\alpha = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta \omega}{\Delta t} = $ ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. If the time interval Δt approaches zero, the instantaneous angular acceleration can be defined as α = limitΔt → 0 (Δω)/(Δt) = (dω)/(dt).

q: The instantaneous angular acceleration is the time rate of change of angular ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Velocity is what this sentence is naming. Velocity is the term used with instantaneous angular acceleration time rate change.

q: When a body is moving with a constant angular acceleration, $\alpha = $ ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. When a body is moving with a constant angular acceleration, α = (ω - ω_0)/(t).

q: Angular acceleration is measured in radian per second squared (rad s$^{-2}$) and revolution per ____ squared (rev s$^{-2}$).
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. Angular acceleration is measured in radian per second squared (rad s^-2) and revolution per second squared (rev s^-2).

q: The magnitude of the angular velocity (angular speed) is related to that of the ____ velocity (tangential speed) as follows.
e: Angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement, dθ/dt. The magnitude of the angular velocity (angular speed) is related to that of the tangential velocity (tangential speed) as follows.

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation between tangential speed and angular speed is $v = $ ____.
e: Circular motion uses angle, ω, and a centre-pointing acceleration v²/r. Since r is constant, the relation between tangential speed and angular speed is v = rω.

q: The relation between the angular acceleration $\alpha$ and the tangential acceleration $a_t$ is $a_t = \frac{dv}{dt} = $ ____.
e: Angular acceleration is the rate of change of angular velocity, dω/dt. The relation between the angular acceleration α and the tangential acceleration a_t is a_t = (dv)/(dt) = (d(rω))/(dt).

q: Since $r$ is constant, the relation simplifies to $a_t = $ ____.
e: Since r is constant, the relation simplifies to a_t = rα. Rα is what this statement is using.

q: In Eq.(1.17), the direction of linear acceleration $a_t$ is ____ to the path.
e: In Eq.(1.17), the direction of linear acceleration a_t is tangential to the path. Tangential is what this statement is using.

q: It is called the ____ acceleration.
e: It is called the tangential acceleration. The name used here is tangential.
